title: Closed [e] — é, -er, -ez, -ed, et, les/des/mes (set 5)
sounds: les / des / mes / tes / ses / ces
focus: All of these make the closed [e]: lips spread, tongue high, a pure « ay » with no glide at the end. It's spelled é; -er, -ez and -ed at the end of a word (parler, chez, pied); the word « et »; and the short words les, des, mes, tes, ses, ces. Exceptions: in a few short words the -er is [ɛʁ] with the r pronounced (mer, fer, hiver, cher, hier), and « est » has the open [ɛ]. Québécois keeps é and è clearly apart, even at the end of a word (« parlé » vs « parlait »).

sentences.fr: Aujourd'hui, nous allons cuisin[er] d[es] crêpes.
sentences.en: Today, we're going to make crepes.

sentences.fr: D'abord, il faut m[é]lang[er] la farine, l[es] œufs [et] le lait.
sentences.en: First, you have to mix the flour, the eggs and the milk.

sentences.fr: Ensuite, vers[ez] un peu de pâte dans la poêle.
sentences.en: Then pour a little batter into the pan.

sentences.fr: Attention : il ne faut pas brûl[er] la crêpe !
À la fin, on met du sirop d'[é]rable. C'est d[é]licieux !
sentences.en: At the end, we add maple syrup. It's delicious!
